text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Friday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- President Guntis Ulmanis does not believe a deal will be struck in Helsinki that will harm the Balts.
- Salaries of the cabinet members increased by an average 200 lats.
- Delegations of Latvia and Russia continue talks on the delimitation of the border, with three sectors of the frontier still to be agreed.
- Parliament voted for a proposal to withdraw immunity from deputy Valdis Krisbergs to be considered at next Monday's meeting.

- Aleksey Vidavski, which is to go on trial for being a member of the Communist party after January 13, 1991, was re-elected mayor of the eastern town of Daugavpils. Aivars Lembergs was re-elected mayor of Ventspils.
- Parliament voted to set up a parliamentary committee to investigate into the squandering of the G-24 loans. The final report of the committee is due until June 1.
- Parliament passed amendments to the law on excise tax, which envisage taxation of medium-strong beer and petroleum.
- Riga heating company has decided to cut off heating supply from its largest debtors, including the Philharmonic Society, hotel Ridzene and hotel Tourist and other buildings.
- The ex-owner of the collapsed bank Baltija, Alexandr Lavent, is likely to be released on bail, which may range between one to 10 million lats.
- Statoil signs an oil terminal building contract with the port of Riga. In the near future it will be also signed by representatives of Neste.
- Latvian hauliers to participate at the international exhibition forum TransRuussia'97 in Moscow.
- The Latvian Development agency to open its representation office in Frankfurt on March 24.
- Swedish ambassador Hans Magnusson said that despite substantial improvements, Swedish businessmen still need to be urged to invest in Latvia.
